question: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about the greatness of Hazrat Imam Hussain (R.A.)?
answer: The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke about the greatness of Hazrat Imam Hussain in many blessed sayings. He declared that Hazrat Fatima is the leader of all women in Paradise, and that Hasan and Hussain are the leaders of all the youngsters in Paradise (Tirmizi: 3781). He also said, "Anyone who loves Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain has indeed loved me, and anyone who hates them has indeed hated me" (Ibn-e-Majah: 143). Once, when the Holy Prophet was going to a feast and saw Imam Hussain in a street of Madinah, he moved forward, stretched out his hand to hold him, and after finally holding him and kissing his forehead, said: "Hussain is from me, and I am from Hussain. Allah loves whoever loves Hussain; Hussain is one of my grandsons" (Ibn-e-Majah: 144). When, in his last days, Hazrat Fatima asked him to bestow something upon her two sons, he said, "We bestowed our awe and leadership to Hassan and valour and generosity to Hussain" (Muajam Kabeer Tabarani 8/185). The Prophet thus made it clear that to love Imam Hussain is to love him, and to keep spite against him is to have spite with the Holy Prophet himself.
explanation: The lesson quotes these hadiths (Tirmizi 3781; Ibn-e-Majah 143 and 144; Muajam Kabeer Tabarani 8/185) while explaining the excellence and greatness of Imam Hussain.

question: What do you know about the event of Karbala? Write down a brief note on it.
answer: After Yazeed seized power, the governor of Madinah Munawwarah, Walid bin Uqbah, called upon Imam Hussain to pledge allegiance to Yazeed, but he refused and left for Makkah, where he stayed for four months. Meanwhile the people of Kufa sent him letters inviting him to Kufa so that they could pledge allegiance to him, saying that they had no leader except him and that under the government of Yazeed Islamic values and commandments were being violated. Imam Hussain therefore sent his paternal cousin, Hazrat Muslim bin Aqeel, to Kufa to assess the situation. When Yazeed learnt of his arrival, he deposed the governor of Kufa, Noman bin Bashir, appointed Ubaidullah bin Ziyad in his place, and ordered that Hazrat Muslim bin Aqeel be killed or made captive; Ibne Ziyad got him martyred. Imam Hussain, with his family, left Makkah for Kufa on 8th Zilhaj, 60 A.H., and after a tiresome journey of twenty-four days arrived at Karbala on 6th Muharram, 61 A.H. The commander of Yazeed's army, Umar bin Saad, insisted that Imam Hussain pledge allegiance to Yazeed, and this communication continued from the 2nd to the 10th of Muharram. Imam Hussain, however, clearly denied the pledge of Yazeed and refused to bow down to falsehood. At last, on 10th Muharram, 61 A.H., a battle between truth and falsehood took place in which Imam Hussain was martyred along with his family and devotees in a state of hunger and thirst. In this way he stood firm to uphold Deen-e-Islam and the superiority of truth, and with his great sacrifice he set an example for the whole Muslim Ummah.
explanation: This follows the lesson's section on the 'Refusal to the pledge of Yazeed and Event of Karbala', covering the dates 8 Zilhaj 60 A.H. and 10 Muharram 61 A.H.

question: Describe the ancestry of Hazrat Imam Hussain (R.A.).
answer: The complete name of Hazrat Imam Hussain is Hussain bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib bin Hashim. His father is Hazrat Ali, the Loin of God, and his mother is Hazrat Fatima Zahra, the daughter of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He is Hashmi from both of his parents and therefore enjoys very high excellence in status. His surname is 'Abu Abdullah' and his titles are 'Sayyid ush Shuhada', 'Sayyid Shabab Ahl al-Jannah' and 'Rayhana tul Nabi'; he is also remembered as 'Shaheed-e-Karbala' in the Muslim Ummah.
explanation: Directly taken from the lesson's 'Ancestry' paragraph, which gives his full lineage, surname and titles.

question: How did Imam Hussain (R.A.) correct the ablution of a man?
answer: Once Hazrat Imam Hussain, along with his brother Imam Hassan, was in a masjid where he saw a man performing ablution improperly. Rather than reproach him directly, he said, "Uncle! We are young and we are offering ablution; please indicate if we make any mistake." When the man saw their ablution, he realised that the two youngsters had performed ablution correctly while his own ablution was incorrect. (Bihar al-anwar, Imam Majlisi, V. 43, pg. 319)
explanation: The lesson narrates this incident as an example of Imam Hussain's high moral character and his gentle manner of correcting others.

question: The last resting place of Imam Hussain (R.A.) is:
answer: Karbala. The lesson states that the shrine of Imam Hussain is located in 'Karbala', a famous city in Iraq, which is his last resting place.
explanation: The lesson's section 'Resting Place' clearly identifies Karbala in Iraq as his final resting place.

answer: 10 Muharram. The lesson states that the battle between truth and falsehood occurred on 10th Muharram 61 A.H., in which Imam Hussain was martyred along with his family and devotees.

question: Give an introduction to the family of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.).
answer: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah's real name was Amir bin Abdullah bin Jarrah bin Hilal. He belonged to 'Banu Fehr', a branch of the Quraish, while his mother, who accepted Islam, belonged to the Banu Harith tribe. His father was killed in the Battle of Badr as an infidel, and because of the grace of Islam he disliked adding the name of his unfaithful father to his own name; hence, with respect to his grandfather, he was referred to as Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
explanation: Taken from the lesson's 'Name and Ancestry' paragraph, which explains his family lineage and why he is known by his grandfather's name. (The exercise prints this section as (A) 'brief answers'; it is recorded here as a short-answer item per the standard section scheme.)

question: When was Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.) born? Why did he attach his name with his grandfather?
answer: He was born in Makkah, in the house of Abdullah bin Jarrah Fehri, after 11 years of Aam ul Feel (the Year of the Elephant), and was brought up in Makkah. He attached his name with his grandfather because his father had been killed in the Battle of Badr as an infidel; out of the grace of Islam he disliked adding the name of his unfaithful father to his own name, and so he was known with reference to his grandfather as Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
explanation: The lesson's 'Birth' and 'Name and Ancestry' sections give his birth (11 years after Aam ul Feel) and the reason for taking his grandfather's name.

question: Why is he called 'Ameen ul Ummah'?
answer: He is called 'Ameen ul Ummah' (the trustworthy of the Ummah) because when the Christians of Najran surrendered and agreed to pay Jizya, they requested the Holy Prophet to send them a trustworthy person. The Holy Prophet held the hand of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah and said, "He is the trustworthy of this Ummah" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, 4380).
explanation: The lesson quotes this hadith of Sahih Al-Bukhari (4380) while explaining his excellence, which gave him the title Ameen ul Ummah.

question: Which event occurred in the battle of Saif ul Bahr for the help of Muslims?
answer: In the expedition to Saif ul Bahr (the sea coast), Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah was sent with a company of Muslims who suffered severe hunger during the campaign. Then, by the help and mercy of Allah, a huge creature of the sea was cast ashore, which the Muslims ate and by means of which they were saved from starvation and were helped; this event is remembered as the divine help granted to the Muslims in the battle of Saif ul Bahr.
explanation: This refers to the well-known expedition of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah to the seashore (Saif ul Bahr) recorded in the hadith literature, where a large sea creature provided relief to the hungry Muslims.

question: Write down an example of the simple lifestyle of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.).
answer: When Ameer ul Momineen Hazrat Umar Farooq once came to his camp, he found nothing with him except a sword and his armour (shield); he said, "(O Abu Ubaidah!) Keep some needful things with you," to which he replied, "O Ameer ul Momineen! Our existing condition of simplicity will lead us to luxurious living very soon" (Musannaf Abdul Razzaq, 11/311). Similarly, after the second conquest of Palestine, when Hazrat Umar came to him for a meal, he presented pieces of dry bread dipped in water, which he was eating himself, showing his extreme simplicity.
explanation: The lesson gives both incidents as examples of his simple, unostentatious lifestyle, citing Musannaf Abdul Razzaq and Sunan Abi Dawood.

answer: Amir. The lesson states that his name was Amir bin Abdullah bin Jarrah bin Hilal.
explanation: The lesson's 'Name and Ancestry' section gives his real name as Amir bin Abdullah bin Jarrah bin Hilal.

question: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.) migrated to two places:
answer: Abyssinia and Madinah. The lesson states that he first migrated to Abyssinia and later migrated to Madinah, thus having the honour of migrating twice for the sake of Allah.

question: The cause of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah's death was:
answer: Epidemic. The lesson states that a plague epidemic broke out in the Muslim cantonment, and its effects spread so widely that thousands of Muslim soldiers were martyred, including Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah, who died in 18 A.H. at the age of 59.
explanation: The lesson's 'Death and Burial' section attributes his death to a plague epidemic.

question: Describe the services of Jabir bin Hayyan in Chemistry.
answer: Jabir bin Hayyan is remembered in Chemistry as 'The Father of Chemistry'. He did a great deal of experiment in medicine and metalwork, discovered many new inventions, and outlined principles of chemistry that are considered authentic till today. He invented an instrument called 'Qura Anbiq' to extract the essence of herbs and flowers by heating, an instrument that is known today as 'Quranfil' (the alembic). He invented sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid, carbonate (Armenic) sulphide, the method of making hair colour, the calcination of metal, and the method of iron varnishing. He was the first chemist to divide matter into three categories - plants, animals and minerals - and he further divided minerals into three types: those that evaporate, those that melt in the fire, and those that erupt on heating. Based on his studies and experiments he also invented a liquid made of elements of different metals and chemical reactions that burned things, which was named 'Tezab' (acid) from 'Tez aab'. In this way a new branch of science, 'Chemistry', was founded, and because of these outstanding services he is honoured as the father of the subject.
explanation: This summarises the lesson's 'Scientific Achievements' section, listing his inventions (Qura Anbiq, acids, calcination, etc.) and his classification of matter.

question: What do you know about the books of Jabir bin Hayyan?
answer: Jabir bin Hayyan is counted among those scholars who wrote a very large number of books. The total number of his booklets and books is more than 232; according to one statement he compiled more than 500 books, most of which have been lost and are not extant today. His books were translated from Arabic into Latin and from Latin into English, and it was through them that Europe approached this knowledge and was introduced to Chemistry. Among his books, 'Aidah', 'Al-Khawas al-Kabir' and 'Al-Meezan' are about Chemistry, while his other books deal with astronomy, physics, geometry, philosophy, logic and politics. (Great Scholars of Chemistry, Jabir bin Hayyan, pg. 20)
explanation: This follows the lesson's 'Books of Jabir bin Hayyan' section, which mentions his more than 232 (or 500) works, their translation, and his chemistry-related books.

question: What do you know about the family and place of birth of Jabir bin Hayyan?
answer: His full name is Jabir bin Hayyan bin Abdullah Kufi, his title is 'Sufi' and his surname is 'Abu Musa'. His ancestors belonged to Khurasan and Tous, and he was born in the tribe Azd in 102 A.H. His father, Hayyan bin Abdullah, had migrated from Syria to Tous and traded in perfume (Itr); Jabir was born a few months after his father opened his perfume shop in Tous, and he acquired his early education there under his father's supervision.
explanation: The lesson's 'Name and Ancestry' and 'Life history' sections give his full name, tribe, year of birth (102 A.H.) and his father's migration to Tous.

question: What was the business of Jabir bin Hayyan's father?
answer: His father, Hayyan bin Abdullah, used to trade in perfume (Itr). After migrating from Syria to Tous because of adverse political and economic conditions, he set up his perfume shop there.
explanation: The lesson states that his father migrated to Tous and started a perfume (Itr) business there.

question: How did Jabir bin Hayyan arrive in Baghdad, and how did people welcome him?
answer: When he reached the age of thirty, Jabir bin Hayyan migrated with his family to the great city of learning (Kufa/Baghdad) to pursue higher knowledge. There he devoted himself to acquiring knowledge of Physics, Mathematics and other subjects; the scholars and the people of learning welcomed and honoured him, and this city became the centre where he carried out his scientific work and experiments.
explanation: The lesson records that at the age of 30 he migrated with his family to Kufa (the great centre of learning of that region) and gave himself to the study of Physics, Mathematics and other sciences.

question: What are the famous inventions of Jabir bin Hayyan?
answer: His famous inventions include the 'Qura Anbiq' (Quranfil), an instrument for extracting the essence of herbs and flowers by heating; sulphuric acid; hydrochloric acid; carbonate (Armenic) sulphide; the method of making hair colour; the calcination of metal; the method of iron varnishing; and the liquid of different metals and chemical reactions that burns things, named 'Tezab' (acid).
explanation: These are the inventions listed in the lesson's 'Scientific Achievements' section.

question: Write down the literary and spiritual services of Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni.
answer: Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni was excellent in spirituality and proficient in Tafseer, Hadith, jurisprudence, Sufism, History, Linguistics and other branches of knowledge, and he was very fond of the Persian and Arabic languages. His interest in reading was so high that he always kept some book in hand, and he maintained a substantial personal library; to develop people's interest in reading he would say, "Whoever buys an expensive book, knowledge would not end from his progeny." He always guided people and invited them toward religion, and in his leisure he busied himself with literary works. His famous books include 'Jama al-Jawami' (a Persian dictionary in four thick volumes), 'Aadab al Murideen', 'Maktoobat', 'Shrah Asma ul Husna' and 'Jamio Sindhi kalam', while his disciples compiled his speeches, quotes and life details in 'Malfoozat Sharif Peer Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni', 'Majma al fiyuzaat' and 'Sohbat nama'. Spiritually, he received his primary training from his father in the Naqshbandiya and then the Qadriya chains, and at the age of 27 he was nominated as the successor of his father. After that he rendered his services in the propagation of Shariah, spirituality, the remembrance of Allah and the spread of the Sunnah. His spiritual compassion benefited thousands; he travelled to Punjab, Kuch Bhooch, Rajhistan, Gujarat, Kathiyawar and Balochistan, benefiting people with knowledge and spiritual excellence. He also worked to eliminate polytheism and innovations in Islam, standing against them in Sindh just as Hazrat Mujaddid Ali Thani and Shah Waliullah Muhaddis Dehlvi had done elsewhere, promoting the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet and illuminating people's hearts with the love of his companions.
explanation: This combines the lesson's 'Spiritual Attachments and Excellence' and 'Literary, Spiritual and military services' sections, listing his books, spiritual chains and preaching services.

question: Why was Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni given the title of 'Raudhe Dhanni'?
answer: It is said that during Ramadan, when Hazrat Muhammad Rashid was an infant, he had a habit of drinking milk at the time of Sehri, and like other fasting persons he would not drink milk throughout the day; then at the time of Maghrib he would go to his mother for milk. Because of this practice of observing the fast from his very infancy, he became famous as 'Roza Dhanni' - the one who fasts. Later on, with reference to his shrine, this name was changed and he became famous as 'Raudhe Dhanni', which means the saint (owner) of a shrine.
explanation: The lesson's birth section explains that his infant habit of fasting gave him the name 'Roza Dhanni', which later became 'Raudhe Dhanni' in association with his shrine.

question: Describe the ancestry of Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni.
answer: His complete name is Syed Muhammad Rashid bin Muhammad Imam Shah, his title is 'Raudhe Dhanni' and his surname is Yaseen. He is the forebear of the famous Syed clan 'Rashidi', and after 36 generations his ancestry reaches Hazrat Imam Hussain bin Ameer ul Momineen Hazrat Ali. The ancestor of his clan was Hazrat Syed Ali Makki, who migrated from his town for the propagation of Islam and settled at 'Lak Aari' near Seewistan (Sehwan), a city of Sindh, because of which the clan became famous as 'Lakyari'. His father, Hazrat Syed Muhammad Baqa Shah Shaheed, was a devout saint and a scholar par excellence of his time.
explanation: The lesson's introduction gives his full name, the 'Rashidi' clan, the descent from Imam Hussain after 36 generations, and the Lakyari settlement of his ancestor Hazrat Syed Ali Makki.

question: From where did Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni get his early education?
answer: Hazrat Syed Muhammad Baqa had set a particular time for the education of his offspring, and he began giving early education to Syed Muhammad Rashid and his siblings at home. Besides his father, Hazrat Muhammad Rashid acquired knowledge from Hafiz Zain Uddin Mahaisr and Mian Muhammad Akram Ghumro, and for further education he was sent to the famous saint of Shikarpur, Shah Faqeerullah Alavi.
explanation: The lesson's 'Education' section states that his early education began at home under his father, along with lessons from Hafiz Zain Uddin Mahaisr and Mian Muhammad Akram Ghumro, and later with Shah Faqeerullah Alavi of Shikarpur.
